Accent: Nigerian English. Tone: warm, clear and upbeat, at a steady natural pace.

Transcript:

lines.c_intro: In many lecture halls, students miss what is taught. Klasync is an assistive platform, so every student can keep up.
lines.s1a: The lecturer signs in and loads the class roster, so attendance is verified against real matric numbers, not a paper register passed around the hall.
lines.s1b: For audio, the lecturer can use the laptop microphone, or a dedicated wireless one for big halls.
lines.s1c: One tap starts a live session, with a join code and a QR code for the projector.
lines.s2a: Students join on their phones with that code, no account, no app. Captions are light text, not video, so they work even with limited data.
lines.s2b: For students with dyslexia or low vision, the screen adapts: larger text, and a dyslexia-friendly font.
lines.s3: The lecture begins, and every word is captioned live, for students who are deaf, hard of hearing, or far from the lecturer.
lines.s4: Students can check in, raise a hand, or send a question. For the shy student, that is a voice, and the lecturer sees it instantly.
lines.s5: A live summary builds as the lecture runs, so anyone who drifts off for a minute can catch up without losing the thread.
lines.s6a: The lecturer can also check understanding on the spot.
lines.s6b: A quick quiz is written from what was just taught. Students answer on their phones, and results arrive live.
lines.s7: When class ends, attendance is scored automatically, so lecturers can spot students who are slipping away, and reach out in time.
lines.t1: After class is where it matters most. A student who was sick, or stuck in transport, signs in and finds the whole lecture waiting.
lines.t2: The transcript is searchable and synced to the recording, so they can replay the exact moment they missed.
lines.t3: Chapters break a long lecture into short parts, so nobody scrubs through two hours for one idea.
lines.t3b: And the summary gives the key points, a quick refresher before a test.
lines.t4: The concept map shows how ideas connect, which helps visual learners. Tap Tour, and it walks through each concept.
lines.t5: For a student who struggles to remember what was taught, from stress, fatigue or ADHD, flashcards turn it into short practice, anywhere.
lines.t6: Then a quiz tests understanding, with instant feedback and an explanation for every answer, so mistakes become learning.
lines.t7: And they can ask the lecture a question. Answers come only from what was said in class, and point to the exact moment.
lines.c_out: Klasync. Inclusive, accessible education for every learner.
